question: In the histogram of heights of 100 male semiprofessional soccer players, what proportion of players are taller than 71.95 inches?

question: In error-based (reduced-error) pruning of a decision tree, what happens when a split would separate a set into a singleton, and how is the label of the resulting leaf chosen?
answer: When a split would produce a singleton, the branch is pruned: the node is turned into a leaf and all branches/nodes below it are removed. The new leaf’s label is chosen by majority vote—the label that occurs most often among the data that reach that node becomes the predicted label for that leaf. In the example, when the split would have produced a singleton, the text says to “make this node a leaf and prune away all branches and nodes underneath it,” and then the node is labeled Red because it contains four red and two blue points. [p323 text]

citations.reading: “Splitting a set into singletons (one-element subsets) is generally not a great idea... One method of pruning is to remove branches that split the data into sets L and R in which one of L or R is a singleton... Then the node becomes a leaf... The label of this new leaf is determined by majority vote. That is, the label that occurs most often becomes the predicted label...”
